title: Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC)
overview: Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) are interconnected disciplines that play a crucial role in modern corporate management. As corporate governance and risk management gain prominence in academic and legislative spheres, the integration of governance, risk, compliance, and internal controls into a unified system becomes essential. Unfortunately, not all organizations recognize the strategic importance of this approach.

This course provides a comprehensive understanding of board structures, committees, and their responsibilities. It also delves into risk management practices aligned with COSO (Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission) guidelines and explores internal controls designed to mitigate risks across various corporate areas. Participants will also gain insights into the latest compliance trends and practices
audience: This course is suitable for board members, senior executives, CFOs, directors, finance managers, legal advisors, corporate secretaries, auditors, HR managers, and department heads who aim to enhance their knowledge of GRC systems.
methodology: The course combines instructor-led presentations with interactive discussions, practical exercises, and real-world case studies to ensure participants can apply the concepts effectively.
competencies: Structuring and analyzing boards of directors and committees.
Enhancing risk monitoring, assessment, and reporting.
Controlling risks and advising on integrated GRC systems.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain corporate governance and its relationship with risk management and internal controls.
Identify the roles and responsibilities of stakeholders in public and private organizations.
Differentiate between governance models and their functions.
Recognize key areas of risk management and the impacts of internal and external environmental changes.
Design and implement effective controls for various business cycles.
